clue.text: American ready to go on the wagon

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and an American dollar is a buck
to board a vehicle is to go on it

explanation.surface: Someone eager to give up drinking, an American ready to go on the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' suggests giving up alcohol, but 'the wagon' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckboard is a light four-wheeled American horse-drawn carriage, a kind of open cart.

clue.text: With a single exception, not quite noble

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: with a single exception means bar one

explanation.surface: A nobleman who is almost, but not entirely, aristocratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a single exception' is BAR ONE; 'not quite' drops the last letter to leave BARON.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the peerage, so a titled nobleman.

clue.text: Go on about horse

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a hunter is a horse bred for fox hunting

explanation.surface: Someone droning on and on about horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To chunter is British slang for muttering or grumbling at length, to keep talking tediously.

clue.text: Stiff young man going round Land's End

indicators.note: going round means the young man's word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a boy is a young male

indicators.note: End means only the final letter of the word Land is taken

explanation.surface: A stiff youth travelling around Land's End in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far south-western tip of Cornwall in England; here it just means the last letter of 'Land'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body.

clue.text: A colleague of Castro is hurt

parts.note: Che Guevara fought alongside Fidel Castro in the Cuban revolution

explanation.surface: A comrade of Fidel Castro has been wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to suffer a dull pain, to hurt.

clue.text: Flora is dug out to identify tree

indicators.note: out signals the letters are dug up and rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A botanist digging up plants to identify a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like plants or a name; with IS and DUG, 'out' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas fir is a tall North American conifer grown for timber.

clue.text: Gaffer not the last with decoration on chest

indicators.note: not the last means the boss word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gaffer is a boss, a foreman
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A foreman wearing a medal pinned on his chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom is a literary word for the chest or breast.

clue.text: Move right outside capital to find pet

indicators.note: outside means the letter for right is placed on the outer side, at the end

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: Relocating outside the capital to find a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar is a small Australian parakeet commonly kept as a cage bird.

clue.text: A diner's battered fish

indicators.note: battered means knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer is served fish in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' looks like fish-and-chip cooking but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The sardine is a small oily sea fish, often tinned.

clue.text: Church leader almost up to date with list that's circulated

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: modern means up to date

indicators.note: circulated means turned round, so the list word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A clergyman nearly modern, handing out a list.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moderator presides over the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland, its chief officer.

clue.text: Series of calls by bore with bad posture

parts.note: a round is a regular series of visits or calls, like a milk round
to shoulder a load is to bear it, so bore is shouldered

explanation.surface: A tedious man making a series of phone calls while slouching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person; it is the past tense of 'bear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone round-shouldered stoops, with shoulders bent forward, a poor posture.

clue.text: Observe distinction

definitions.meaning: eminence, as in a person of ...

explanation.definitionFit: Note means to notice, and a person of note has distinction or importance.

clue.text: Fish taken back to jetty more likely to be a kipper?

definitions.text: more likely to be a kipper?

indicators.note: taken back means the fish word is read backwards

parts.note: eels are fish
a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: Fish brought back to the jetty, perhaps destined to become kippers.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, which suits the fishy surface; here it means someone having a kip, a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Kip is British slang for sleep, so one more likely to kip is sleepier.

clue.text: Send for the auditor — king reveals main losses

parts.note: to ship goods is to send them

indicators.note: for the auditor means the word is what a listener hears

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, as used in royal signatures

explanation.surface: An accountant is summoned and a king reveals heavy losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant but means a listener; 'main' is the sea, not chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is the open sea, so ships lost at sea are main losses.

clue.text: Cops — insert rank

indicators.note: rank means foul or corrupt, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to put in police officers of a certain grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a police grade, which it also is here.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors are police officers of a particular grade, so cops of a rank.

clue.text: County going after car dealers

indicators.note: going after means the county follows the car

parts.note: Merc is short for a Mercedes car
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A county following behind a car dealership.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchants are traders, people who buy and sell goods.

clue.text: Service area retaining the same flipping means of communication

indicators.note: retaining means the service and area words hold the next piece inside

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: idem is Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A motorway service area keeps the same annoying communications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass media are press, radio and television, channels reaching the public at large.

clue.text: Write about city centre without bungling

indicators.note: without means outside, so the centre letters surround the next piece
centre means the middle letters of the word city
about means the word for write is turned round

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Writing about the city centre without making a mess of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' here, but in older English it means 'outside', so the city's centre letters wrap round the reversed word for write.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or incompetent, so blundering.

clue.text: Soak too much

explanation.definitionFit: To steep is to soak in liquid, and a steep price is an excessive one.

clue.text: Surround club after sin? Not entirely

indicators.note: after means the club goes behind the sin
not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: envy is one of the seven deadly sins
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer surrounded by jealousy after a sinful swing.
explanation.definitionFit: To environ is to encircle or enclose something, an old-fashioned verb.

clue.text: Soldier extremely rude about armed vessel

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

indicators.note: about means those outer letters are turned round
extremely means the outer letters of the word rude

explanation.surface: A soldier being very rude about a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned ship authorised to attack enemy vessels in war.

clue.text: Bar constraining river passage

indicators.note: constraining means holding in, so the river letter goes inside

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A barrier holding back a river's passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a barrier or pub; it is the preposition meaning 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short passage taken from a book, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Independent state entertained by Jagger?

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside the singer's name

parts.note: Mick Jagger is the Rolling Stones singer
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A state entertained by a Rolling Stones frontman.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an unorthodox, independent-minded person who goes their own way.

clue.text: Fiddle starts to sound clear as mud

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A violin begins to sound murky.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is slang for a swindle or fraud, a dishonest scheme.

clue.text: Athlete once taking part in preliminary round

indicators.note: round means the run is turned backwards
taking part in means a run of letters is found inside the word

explanation.surface: A runner from the past competing in an early heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a heat of a race but signals the reversal of RELIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A miler is a runner over the mile distance, a race now rarely run since metrication.

clue.text: Old Greek and English monster

explanation.surface: A beast that is part ancient Greek, part English.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a fearsome creature.

clue.text: Wader that may be found in wood

definitions.meaning: a wading bird of the sandpiper family

definitions.text: that may be found in wood
definitions.meaning: a hard dark spot in timber where a branch grew

explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a shore bird, and a knot is also a hard spot in timber.

clue.text: Straight men with blanket for head

parts.note: direct means straight
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
blanket means general, as in blanket coverage

explanation.surface: Straight men wrapped in a blanket to keep their heads warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blanket' looks like bedding but is the adjective meaning all-covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A director-general is the chief executive of a large organisation, such as the BBC.

clue.text: Times providing cover for new saint

indicators.note: providing cover for means wrapping round the next piece

parts.note: ages are long times

explanation.surface: A newspaper providing cover for a new saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means long periods.
explanation.definitionFit: St Agnes is an early Christian virgin martyr of Rome.

clue.text: One sees record producer first of all with time inside

indicators.note: inside means these letters go within the producer's name

parts.note: Phil Spector was a famous American record producer

indicators.note: first of means the first letter of the word all

explanation.surface: A record producer's first priority is to put in the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is someone watching an event, an onlooker.
